title: Cipher and Letter
premise: Rafael Fairweather, the reclusive estate lawyer of Hollowmere, is summoned to probate a will for Edith Vane—a woman who died thirty years ago, or so everyone believed. When her 'widower' is found dead wearing clothes lifted from Rafael's own closet, Rafael becomes both suspect and investigator, forced to confront the identity they buried two decades ago. As alibis unravel and old letters surface, Rafael discovers Edith faked her death to escape a conspiracy among the town's founding families—one that now needs Rafael silenced. In the end, Rafael chooses exposure over invisibility, testifying at last and finding family not in blood but in the unlikely allies who stand beside them.
about_author: Yara Blackwood is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the private papers of small-town estates before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who hide in plain sight, from a cottage she refuses to geotag.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A courier delivers a probate request for Edith Vane, dead since 1994, bearing Rafael's own notary seal—used only once, twenty years ago, on a night Rafael has tried to forget. The emotional beat is dread: the past has found a filing error, and it's addressed to them.

chapters.title: Hollowmere's Best-Kept Man
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with flashbacks. We see Rafael's meticulously ordered life: alphabetized case files, no photographs, no visitors. A brief memory surfaces of a rain-soaked night when someone begged Rafael to witness a document. Beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Detective Imogen Sark's POV. Gerald Vane, Edith's husband, is found strangled in the chapel ruins—dressed head to toe in clothing stolen from Rafael's closet. Rafael becomes the prime suspect. Beat: terror as invisibility collapses overnight.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibi
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV under interrogation. Every town elder offers Gerald an airtight alibi dated to the same week in 1994—the week Edith died. Rafael realizes the alibis were rehearsed, coordinated. Beat: the cold clarity of realizing a whole town is lying in unison.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Forensics dates the stolen clothes' removal to hours before the murder—someone was inside Rafael's home. Imogen privately doubts Rafael's guilt but can't say why. Beat: wary alliance forming between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: Letters in the Lining
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Searching Edith's sealed effects, Rafael finds letters sewn into a coat lining—written to 'R.F., my witness, my friend.' Edith knew Rafael before the will, before the amnesia Rafael claims. Beat: vertigo; identity itself begins to feel like a forged document.

chapters.title: The Founding Families Dinner
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, Rafael's POV. Rafael attends the annual Ashcombe Trust dinner, watching five families perform grief for Gerald while exchanging glances like signals. Old matriarch Constance Hale warns: 'Stop reading, start burning.' Beat: menace dressed in charity.

chapters.title: What Rafael Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, Rafael's POV. Twenty years ago, a young Rafael witnessed a document declaring Edith dead—and took payment in silence, erasing their own name from every record afterward. Beat: shame finally named; the mystery turns inward.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Constance Hale is found drowned in her own ornamental pond, a page of Edith's letters weighted in her pocket. The killer is cleaning house faster than Rafael can read. Beat: escalating dread; the letters are now a death sentence.

chapters.title: An Unlikely Constable
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Imogen confronts Rafael off the record; Rafael shares one letter, gambling on her integrity. Imogen reveals Gerald's death certificate was signed by a doctor who left town in 1995. Beat: trust, fragile and deliberate, against duty.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Daughter
chapters.summary: New POV: Wren Okafor, a young mortuary assistant who has quietly idolized Rafael for years. Wren admits her father was the signing doctor—and that he left behind a sealed confession she's never dared open. Beat: found family's first true hand extended.

chapters.title: Confession, Sealed and Yellowed
chapters.summary: Wren and Rafael's shared POV. The confession reveals Edith didn't die—she was smuggled out after discovering the Trust laundered its fortune through fake deaths, including her own staged one. Beat: revelation and grief; Rafael's silence made them complicit.

chapters.title: Someone Is in the House
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, night scene. Returning home, Rafael finds the office ransacked, the remaining letters gone, and a fresh cup of tea still warm on the desk—an intimate threat. Beat: violation; the killer knows Rafael's rituals better than anyone alive.

chapters.title: The Understudy
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Suspicion falls on Julian Marsh, the Trust's charming solicitor, whose handwriting matches annotations on the stolen letters. But his alibi for Constance's death is genuine—which means he isn't the killer, just another keeper of secrets. Beat: misdirection resolved, deeper rot exposed.

chapters.title: Edith, Alive and Waiting
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Following a clue in the letters' watermarks, Rafael drives to a coastal convent and finds Edith Vane—old, sharp, and furious that Rafael waited twenty years to come. Beat: confrontation between the woman who ran and the witness who hid.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Edith and Rafael's alternating POV. Edith confesses she once loved Rafael and asked them to witness her 'death' believing it would free them both; Rafael's self-erasure was never what she intended. Beat: love confessed too late, duty examined and refused.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Chapel
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. A note lures Rafael back to the chapel ruins where Gerald died. Imogen, tailing secretly, realizes the killer wants Rafael dead wearing Rafael's own clothes again—to close the frame permanently. Beat: the trap springs shut.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Names
chapters.summary: Climax part one, Rafael's POV. The killer is revealed: Mrs. Abernathy, the Trust's elderly registrar, who has falsified every death record for forty years and killed to keep the ledger clean. She believes she is the town's guardian angel. Beat: banality of evil, face to face.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax part two, ensemble POV. Abernathy forces Rafael at knifepoint to certify one final false death—Rafael's own. Instead, Rafael speaks aloud, on record, every secret they've kept, as Imogen closes in. Beat: courage as choosing to be seen.

chapters.title: After the Verdict
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Abernathy is arrested; the Trust's families scatter under investigation. Imogen clears Rafael formally and, over terrible coffee, asks to hear the whole story someday—not as a detective, but as a friend. Beat: relief and the first breath of belonging.

chapters.title: Probate at Last
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael executes Edith's real will, dissolving the Trust and returning its wealth to the descendants it was stolen from—including Wren. Edith watches from the back of the courtroom, and for the first time, Rafael doesn't look away. Beat: restitution, legal and personal.

chapters.title: Cipher and Letter
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Rafael's POV. One year later: Rafael's office has photographs on the walls now, Sunday dinners with Wren and Imogen, and a framed letter from Edith beginning 'To R.F., who stayed.' Rafael files the last document of the Vane case and locks nothing. Beat: peace earned; identity chosen, not hidden.
